epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #32049 (G1 part (d), `Fixes #31691`) at head e57ec3eb: PASS.** It lands once CI is green and the seat ACCEPTs.

- **Red line 1, never loosen: holds.** The second allow-list row is purely syntactic: five segments, `POST` only, and `:ns` is never `runs`. Every address it admits is either refused with the door's one answer before the body is read, or served as the bare hook for the same `(flowName, hookId)`. The bare hook still needs the same HMAC signature. So no request gets anything the bare door would not already give a sender who can sign. The run doors of a flow named `hooks` (`POST /automation/hooks/runs/:runId/*`) keep their gates on both faces: the hosted row never matches them, and the mount calls `next()`. The conformance pin derives the exclusion set from the route ledger, so a new route of that shape fails the build rather than slipping through.
- **Red line 2, never guess: holds.** Admission reads the engine's own `packagedFlowOwner` and the registry's namespace table, and core's single predicate (`admitInboundHookAddress`) judges both faces. An engine that cannot answer admits no address, which is fail-closed. `_env` is served only for a flow no package ships, and a packaged flow's environment overlay stays that package's item (D4). The refusal is core's one rendering, so its status, headers and bytes equal a bad signature's. It never answers `404` or `409`, which means the response gives no namespace-enumeration oracle. The cause is written only to the log, and both faces have pins for that.
- **Red line 3, independently releasable: holds.** The PR is `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and moves only paths that were unserved before (404 or 401 becomes the hook's answer), and the changeset declares every change. The `runs` limit has a first-party count of 0. Moving `INVALID_SIGNATURE` to the core row in the error-code ledger changes provenance only.

**Non-blocking.** The hosted row compares the raw segment, so `r%75ns` is not excluded there. It reaches the hook door, which decodes it to `runs` and refuses it (401). The mount decodes the segment first and calls `next()`. Neither face loosens anything.

**Carry-in for B #31696, recorded here:** the qualified hook reaches the one flow the engine arms per bare name. Once #31696 arms flows by `(package, name)`, the qualified address must dispatch to the named holder's own hook, and the predicate must become "the namespace holds a flow of this name". Otherwise the qualified and bare addresses will name different things. B #31696 owns that change, and it is not owed here.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e57ec3eb7e200f3c7185a6574d98dbd8ca8d4cbf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/core/src/security/auth-gate.ts, packages/core/src/security/inbound-hook-answer.ts, packages/core/src/security/anonymous-deny.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/index.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/trigger-api-route-ledger.ts (the seat's security-face widening: the whole non-test source of the diff)

Inputs read: card #31691 (body and all 7 comments, rulings 6754822117 included), the PR body, the 22-file list, the net diff `origin/main...e57ec3eb`, and the head's check-runs. Code outside the diff was read at the head to judge it: `ApiTrigger.handleRequest`, `serveInboundHook`, `handleAutomationRequest`'s floor and hand-off, `AutomationEngine.packagedFlowOwner`, `SchemaRegistry.getNamespaceOwners`, `NAMESPACE_POSITION_LITERALS`.

Check-runs at render time: none failed, and many had no conclusion yet (the Test Core and Test UI shards, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, the Type Check families other than source gates, and Lint · CI/release/engine, · repo and tooling, · scoped slot lookup). Concluded green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness. The runs still open carry the gate verdicts this record cannot read; the PASS below is the design verdict and does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Anonymous accept-set (ADR-0069 allow-list, the `/automation` floor, the membership skip).** Grows by exactly `POST` + five segments `automation/hooks/:ns/:flowName/:hookId`, one optional `/environments/:id`, no empty segment, raw compare, `:ns` not `runs`. Right. All three readers go through `matchParameterisedRoute`, so the `except` applies to each. Six segments, a mount base, other methods and `runs` stay gated.
- **`runs` exclusion.** Right, and it is the whole set: the only five-segment `POST /automation` ledger rows other than the hook and `connectors/:ns/:name/connection` are `:name/runs/:runId/cancel|resume|restore-suspension`. `hooks` is a refused namespace literal on the automation door, so no addressed row reads `hooks` as a namespace. Excluding `runs` in the qualifier position, not the three verbs, also keeps `POST hooks/runs/r1/screen` at the domain's 405.
- **Public surface.** `@objectstack/core` gains `INBOUND_HOOK_QUALIFIER_EXCLUSIONS`, `INBOUND_HOOK_REFUSAL_STATUS`, `inboundHookRefusal`, `inboundHookJsonResponse`, `inboundHookRefusalResponse`, `admitInboundHookAddress`, `InboundHookAddress`, and an optional `qualifier` on `InboundHookRouteMatch`; `@objectstack/trigger-api` gains `HOOKS_ADDRESSED_PATH` and `ApiTrigger.refuseUnadmittedAddress`. All additive. Right.
- **Answer changes.** As the PR declares, and only on paths no route served: mounted host `404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND` to the hook door's answer; catch-all host the anonymous `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` and the signed-in no-route answer to the same. No served route narrows. Right.
- **Error-code provenance.** `INVALID_SIGNATURE` leaves the trigger-api row and joins the core row; the literal is now stamped only at `packages/core/src/security/inbound-hook-answer.ts:50`, and `packages/triggers/trigger-api/src` holds it in prose only. Union, casing and status unchanged; no waiver. Right. (`check:error-code-provenance` rides a Lint family still running.)
- **Route ledgers.** One `public` row in the runtime ledger (census 147 to 148) and one `server-only` row in the trigger ledger; both describe the code as written. Right.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on core, trigger-api and runtime, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, in both the PR body and the changeset. Correct under the repo rule (a `none` kind ships `patch`; a non-protocol widening ships `patch`). `packages/spec` moves a provenance row only and sits in the fixed group with core and runtime. Check Changeset concluded success.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — agreed. The one declared limit (a `runs` namespace has no qualified hook, first-party 0) is a limit on the new surface, not a narrowing of a served one.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Names** (`inbound-hook-answer.ts`, `admitInboundHookAddress`, `inboundHookRefusal`, `inboundHookJsonResponse`, `inboundHookRefusalResponse`, `InboundHookAddress`, `INBOUND_HOOK_QUALIFIER_EXCLUSIONS`, `HOOKS_ADDRESSED_PATH`, `refuseUnadmittedAddress`, cause `unadmitted-address`): accepted. No new error code.
- **The `runs` namespace**: the declared limit is accepted for this PR. Adding `runs` to `NAMESPACE_POSITION_LITERALS.inboundHook` is a `packages/spec` edit and an install narrowing; it goes on a follow-up card, which should also settle nit 3 below.
- **The spec contract** (`ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook` carries no qualifier): accepted. The member keys a hook by the bare flow name, the hosted face judges the qualifier before it calls the member, and both faces ask the one predicate.
- **Seat rulings on part (d)** (6754822117 and the C2 step-0 ruling): one 401 renderer and the predicate in core, trigger-api calls it — held; byte equality pinned on both faces — held; the reason in the log only — held; `runs` excluded in `auth-gate.ts` — held; "never 404 or 409" — held.
- **Carry-ins on the card** (U's pair-addressed read, E4's activation 409, B's agent and skill qualified read): each is pinned on `main` by parts (a) and (c), so `Fixes #31691` closes nothing owed.
- **Check-runs**: the runs listed above have no conclusion yet. Landing waits for them.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged as an attacker would, per the seat's six questions.

1. **Can an unsigned or wrongly signed request reach a handler, a flow or a row write?** No. An admitted address is handed to the same `serveInboundHook` / `ApiTrigger.handleRequest` as the bare route, with the bare flow name and hook id; the hook match, the per-hook secret and the verifier all run before anything is parsed or enqueued. The admission only removes addresses, it adds no path around the verifier. Near shapes: four and six segments, an empty segment, a mount base, other verbs and `runs` (scoped too) do not match the row; an encoded slash stays one raw segment, decodes to a name nothing holds and is refused; case differs from every literal and is refused or gated. The hand-off in `automation.ts` is the statement after the floor and reads the same `matchInboundHookRoute`, so the floor and the branch cannot disagree.
2. **Is the refusal byte-equal on both faces?** Yes for status, headers and body. Hosted: `inboundHookRefusalResponse()` against the member's `inboundHookJsonResponse(inboundHookRefusal())`, both returned as `result`. Mount: `c.json(refusal.body, refusal.status)` against `serveInboundHook`'s `c.json`, the body from the one `inboundHookRefusal()`. The absent-slot `501` is answered before the admission on the hosted face, so it does not tell addresses apart. But see finding 1: the answer is equal, the moment it is sent is not.
3. **Does the cause reach the log only?** Yes. The message text is constant and the caller's strings go in structured fields only; the body is core's fixed object.
4. **Constant-time compare over the raw body, secret per hook?** Unchanged by this diff and still true: `safeEqual` on the hook id, `verifyHttpSignature` / `verifyDeclaredSignature` over `rawBody`, the secret read from the armed hook of that flow. The engine arms one flow per bare name, so a qualified address reaches exactly the hook the bare route reaches; one package's secret cannot admit another's hook through the qualifier.
5. **Does `runs` stay outside the hook gate?** Yes: `matchParameterisedRoute` returns no match, so the floor denies an anonymous caller and a signed-in caller falls through to the run door; the mount calls `next()` before reading anything.
6. **Provenance move.** Matches the stamp site (① above).

Findings:

- **1 — should-fix. The refusal is equal in bytes but not in when it is sent, and that tells an admitted address from an unadmitted one without any signature.** Both faces judge the qualifier before the body is read (`plugin.ts`, the `HOOKS_ADDRESSED_PATH` handler; `automation-hooks.ts`, the `hook.qualifier` block), and answer an unadmitted address at once. An admitted address goes on to `serveInboundHook`, whose first statement awaits the whole request body. The bare route reads the body for every post, known flow or not, so it has no such difference; the qualified route introduces it. A caller who declares a body and withholds it sees the two cases apart, with no statistics needed, and so learns for a guessed pair whether that namespace is installed and ships a flow of that name (and, through `_env`, whether a name is a packaged flow). That is the existence signal the part (d) ruling's "never 404 or 409" and the changeset's "tells no installed namespace from another" exist to withhold. The letter of the rulings is met (they name status, headers and bytes), so this is not graded must-fix; the impact is an install fingerprint, never an admission. The same ordering puts the refusal ahead of the hosted face's `bodyUsed` 500 and its member-throw 500, so on a faulting transport an unadmitted address answers 401 where an admitted one answers 500. Fix: make an unadmitted address cost what the bare route's unknown flow costs — read the body before answering the refusal (or judge the address after the body read, beside the member's `unknown-flow` arm), and on the hosted face run the `bodyUsed` check before the admission. The prose that states "before the body or the signature is read" (changeset, both ledger rows, three docblocks) moves with it. A pin: a post whose body never arrives gets no answer on either an admitted or an unadmitted address.
- **2 — nit. The two faces log different fields for the same cause.** The hosted face logs `{ cause, flowName, qualifier }`; the mount logs `{ cause, flowName }` through `refuseUnverified`, so on a self-hosted kernel the one record of the cause does not carry the qualifier that caused it.
- **3 — nit. The `runs` limit is read raw by the allow-list and decoded by the hosted face.** `except` compares the raw segment; `automation-hooks.ts` then decodes the qualifier. A percent-escaped spelling of `runs` therefore passes the row and, on a host with a package whose namespace is `runs`, is judged as that namespace, where the mount's router decodes first and passes the request on. Every such post still needs the hook's signature, and no run door reads the escaped spelling, so nothing is exposed; the declared limit ("a `runs` namespace has no qualified inbound hook") is just not exact on the hosted face. Refusing `runs` at install (the follow-up in ③) removes it.
- **4 — nit. The exclusion pin reads one row shape.** `route-ledger.conformance.test.ts` collects only rows with a literal second segment and a parameter third. A future `POST /automation/:name/x/y/:z` row would collide with the qualified hook for a flow named `hooks` and the pin would not see it. Accepted as a follow-up; no such row exists.
- **5 — nit. `inboundHookRefusal()`'s docblock and the ledger comment say "every post the door does not serve gets ONE answer".** The member still answers `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` to a post naming an armed flow and its hook id while the secret cannot be read. Pre-existing and stated in `handleRequest`; the new prose is slightly wider than the code.

The `hits` file, `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`: the move holds against the code it cites (the stamp site, both wire paths named in the comment) and against its consumer, the provenance gate. No finding.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `be3857682089183364e3432b838d1d6cec79af2f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts, packages/core/src/security/inbound-hook-answer.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/trigger-api-route-ledger.ts, their tests (automation-hooks.test.ts, inbound-hook-member.test.ts, route-ledger.conformance.test.ts), .changeset/31691-qualified-inbound-hook.md. The PR's own change since e57ec3eb is e1d81bf6 + be385768; fb451c76 merges `main` and touches none of this PR's files' hunks under review.

Delta review of the record on head e57ec3eb (PASS, one should-fix S1, four nits). The PR body is patched to r2 by the seat and read back identical.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **S1 is closed.** An unadmitted qualified address now answers only after its body has been read in full, on both faces. The admitted path also reads the whole body before it answers, so a sender who withholds the body gets no answer on either. The time to answer no longer tells an installed namespace (or a packaged flow name, via `_env`) from an uninstalled one.
   - Hosted face (`handleInboundHookRequest`): the `bodyUsed` 500 now runs before admission, so a consumed body is the same 500 on admitted and unadmitted addresses. The unadmitted arm reads `request.text()`. If that read throws, the answer is `memberFaultAnswer`, the same sanitised 500 the member's own fault gives, with the cause in the log.
   - Mount (`ApiTriggerPlugin`): `await c.req.text()` runs before `refuseUnadmittedAddress`. A failed read there fails the same way as `serveInboundHook`'s own read on an admitted address.
   - The member-throw 500 cannot be ordered before admission, because an unadmitted address never reaches the member. What both arms share is the transport-fault 500, and that now matches.
   - Pins (runtime and trigger-api, `_env` included): a withheld body gets no answer on either arm, and each arm gets its own answer once the body closes. Consumed and mid-read-failed bodies give the same 500 on both.
2. **The answers are unchanged:** status, headers and bytes are the same as on e57ec3eb. Only the time the refusal is sent moves. No accept set moves.
3. **N2 is closed.** The mount's refusal log now carries `qualifier` beside `cause` and `flowName`, as the hosted face's does. Pinned. No secret, signature or body is logged.
4. **N4 is closed.** The exclusion pin now covers every five-segment `POST /automation` row whose first segment can read `hooks`. It fails if any such row has a parameter in the qualifier position. It was ablated with a new `POST /automation/:name/x/y/:z` row and went red.
5. **The prose follows the code.** "Before the body or the signature is read" now reads "judged before the signature is read, answered once the body is read in full" in the changeset, both ledger rows and the docblocks.
6. **Ablations (thread report):** all 5 went red: hosted body read (2), `bodyUsed` order (1), mount body read (1), log qualifier (1), new ledger row (1).

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right: `patch` on core, trigger-api and runtime; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; `Metadata-protocol: none`. The ledger's `INVALID_SIGNATURE` provenance move (seat ruling A) is unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

- N3 (refusing `runs` as a namespace at install) goes to the ADR amendment card the seat files after this lands. N5 is existing behaviour, left as it is.
- The epic seat's red-line read on e57ec3eb was PASS. This round moves only when the refusal is sent and adds a log field, which is inside those red lines.
- Gates (thread report, r2):
  - build 70/70.
  - core 3271, trigger-api 67, runtime 9361 tests.
  - tsc clean on all three.
  - dogfood 4 files, 98 tests.
  - 98/98 derived gates, 0 NOT-MEASURED. `check:optional-error-sink` was red and is fixed in be385768.

### ④ Design judgment

No new finding. Admission itself (the namespace-table read) still runs before the body is read. Its cost is a local lookup, the same order as the member's own flow lookup, and much smaller than the body read that S1 removed as an oracle.

Check-runs on this head were still running when this record was written. Landing waits for them to finish all green.
